reason: Both tools strongly agree on the top candidate (Cohen syndrome): PCF rank 1 score 1.0 and GM rank 1 distance 0.627 (best) / score 0.518. After ~PCF rank 6 scores remain high but are already broad NDD syndromes; incremental ranks beyond 6 (scores ~0.823 and below) add many nonspecific neurodevelopmental syndromes with diminishing marginal value. GM shows a relatively steep drop from rank 1 (0.627) to ranks 2–6 (0.664–0.695), but ranks 2–6 still represent plausible, distinct facial gestalt syndromes (e.g., pontocerebellar hypoplasia, Coffin-Siris, Kabuki, Usmani-Riazuddin, Shashi-Pena) and add coverage not mirrored exactly by PCF. Beyond GM rank 6, distances worsen gradually (>=0.695) with many generic NDD entries, so keeping more offers limited additional discriminatory coverage under the review budget. Total retained = 12 <= 20.
